title: Revamping of Control System for Alkylation and Aromatic
client: Aradet (The Arab Company for Detergent Chemicals)

phases.title: Site survey, legacy audit and I/O freeze
steps: Collect as-built loop drawings, cause-and-effect charts and P&IDs for the Alkylation and Aromatic units; log revision status.
Walk down marshalling and RIO cabinets; check terminal numbers and cable tags against loop drawings; record discrepancies.
Export the legacy DCS/PLC I/O list; map each signal to a PCS 7 channel with type, range and engineering unit.
Extract existing CFC/SFC charts and control logic; classify each as migrate, rewrite or retire.
Freeze the tag and I/O lists under change control; issue revision A as the migration baseline.
Check hazardous-area loops: IS barrier or isolator rating, entity parameters, cable capacitance and inductance.
Record the legacy network: PROFIBUS addresses, baud rate, repeaters, IP plan and VLANs.
Back up legacy projects, configurations and historian data to offline media; checksum and sign off.
Identify trip and critical loops; agree bypass, override and forcing rules with operations.
Hold a survey review covering risks, outage windows, spares and long-lead items; get client approval of the freeze.

phases.title: Hardware engineering and panel integration
steps: Create the multiproject in SIMATIC Manager; define the plant hierarchy for each unit.
In HW Config insert the S7-410H station with two racks; set rack numbers 0 and 1 and CPU firmware per the PCS 7 release matrix.
Insert sync modules and connect two fiber sync links between the CPUs; route the cables separately.
Insert a CP 443-5 Extended per CPU as DP master and a CP 443-1 with fixed IP addresses.
Set H-system parameters: cycle monitoring time, minimum I/O retention time and maximum communication delay.
Configure remote I/O stations (ET 200M with IM 153-2, or ET 200SP HA) with redundant interface modules.
Assign every module and channel; enable diagnostic, wire-break and short-circuit alarms.
Design redundant 24 VDC supplies with redundancy modules or diodes; add supply monitoring to diagnostics.
Build and inspect panels: wiring, ferrules, torque, shield terminations, earthing and labels per drawings.
Run pre-power checks: insulation test, continuity, supply polarity and segregation of IS circuits.
Compile HW Config, run the consistency check and archive the project revision.

phases.title: Redundant PROFIBUS DP and network management
steps: Define redundant DP master systems: CP 443-5 Ext in Rack 0 drives Line A, Rack 1 drives Line B.
Allocate PROFIBUS addresses (masters 1-2, slaves from 3); freeze the address table and check for duplicates.
Set baud rate by segment length: 12 Mbps up to 100 m, 1.5 Mbps up to 200 m on type A cable; use the same DP bus profile in all nodes.
Configure Y-Links for single-channel devices; verify both IM 153-2 interfaces and the subordinate DP subnet address.
Fit terminators at segment ends only, powered; add repeaters or OLMs where segment limits require.
Test cables with a bus tester: continuity, shield, A/B swap and terminated-segment resistance (about 110 ohm), before connecting devices.
Run a live-list scan; confirm every station is present and record signal quality.
Configure the SCALANCE MRP ring: one manager, all others clients; set the recovery time per specification.
Configure SINEC NMS: discover topology, add devices, set SNMPv3 credentials, thresholds and trap receivers.
Harden the network: disable unused ports and services, enable port security, replace default credentials.
Back up switch configurations and record firmware versions.

phases.title: PCS 7 AS/OS and redundant SCADA engineering
steps: Create the PCS 7 library and import the required APL version; compare with legacy using Version Cross Manager.
Define the plant hierarchy and technological names; create process tag types for repeated equipment.
Migrate CFC charts: instantiate APL blocks, connect I/O through channel drivers, set runtime groups and OB cycles.
Migrate SFC sequences; verify steps, transitions, interlocks and operator modes.
Compile the AS and clear all messages; download in STOP to the first CPU, then bring up redundancy.
Configure the OS servers: OS project editor, partner server for OS_SRV_B, redundancy and archive synchronization.
Set up Tag Logging and Alarm Logging: archives, sizes, message classes and horn assignment.
Build Alkylation and Aromatic graphics: P&IDs, faceplates, navigation and trend groups.
Generate server data and load it on each OS client; test every client against both servers.
Configure time synchronization: NTP or SICLOCK as master for the AS and OS.
Configure user roles and authorization levels with SIMATIC Logon; test operator rights.
Back up the AS and OS projects and tag them as the FAT baseline.

phases.title: FAT and iFAT
steps: Prepare the FAT procedure, I/O simulators, test equipment and witness sign-off sheets.
Simulate 100% of AI, AO, DI and DO channels per the I/O list, including ranges and alarms.
Test CFC/SFC logic: interlocks, trip matrix, sequence steps and fault handling.
Force CPU-0 to STOP and measure the output disturbance; accept switchover under 50 ms with no bump.
Reverse the test (master to CPU-1 and back); confirm resync and that REDF clears.
Remove one sync fiber; confirm the system stays redundant on the other link and diagnostics are raised.
Break PROFIBUS Line A, then Line B; confirm no slave drops and diagnostic alarms appear.
Fail OS Server A, then B: check client reconnection, alarm continuity and archive sync after restart.
Break one MRP ring link; confirm recovery within the configured time and the NMS trap.
Remove one 24 VDC feed; confirm no loss of function and a supply alarm.
Stop the NTP/SICLOCK master; verify behaviour and recovery of time synchronization.
Close the punch list, freeze the FAT software, create the SAT baseline and archive.

phases.title: Hot cutover, loop checking and SAT
steps: Issue a cutover method statement per unit with a rollback plan and decision points.
Obtain permits, lock-out and isolation certificates; hold a toolbox talk with operations.
Install and power the new cabinets; validate supplies and communications before touching field wiring.
Tie in in order: spare loops, non-critical loops, then critical loops, one group at a time.
Cut over cross-wiring at marshalling loop by loop; label and photograph each change.
Loop check end to end: 4-20 mA with a calibrator, HART communicator checks, digital inputs and outputs.
Verify alarm limits, scaling and failure states (open circuit, short circuit) per loop.
Verify interlocks and the trip matrix on the live plant under operations supervision.
Repeat key redundancy tests on site: CPU, PROFIBUS, OS server and ring.
Run the 72-hour reliability test; log alarms, diagnostics and redundancy events with none unexplained.
Train operators; hand over documents, backups, credentials, spares and as-built drawings.
Obtain SAT and handover sign-off from Aradet.

All configured slaves in data exchange; no diagnostics
Red/green not swapped; continuity verified per core
Measured loss within the sync module datasheet budget; connectors cleaned
Both links up; IFM1F and IFM2F off
RACK0 and RACK1 LEDs match HW Config
One CPU master (MSTR on), one standby, REDF off
Under 50 ms; outputs without bump; measured with a scope
Identical on both CPUs; matches the PCS 7 release matrix
Load and work memory identical; consistency check passed
Cycle monitoring, min I/O retention time, communication delay as designed

Operator, supervisor and engineer roles tested and logged

runbook.title: PROFIBUS and OB diagnostics
rows: OB82
Diagnostic interrupt: channel or module fault. Read the diagnostic buffer or SFC 13; fix wire break, short or module.
OB83
Module inserted or removed. Verify type, reseat, and confirm parameters were reloaded.
OB86
Rack or DP station failure. Check slave power, connector, terminator and address.
OB122
I/O access error. Check address, slot and bus; read the start information of the OB.
OB70
I/O redundancy error (H). Check the DP line and IM 153-2 on the lost path.
OB72
CPU redundancy error. Check sync links, then the diagnostic buffer for the cause.
OB121
Programming error. Find the called block in the start information and correct it.

runbook.title: S7-410H LED states
rows: RUN on, MSTR on, REDF off
Master CPU, redundant. Normal.
RUN on, MSTR off, REDF off
Standby CPU, redundant. Normal.
REDF on
Redundancy lost. Check IFM1F/IFM2F, then versions and diagnostic buffer.
IFM1F on
Sync interface 1 fault. Check fiber, clean connectors, swap sync module.
IFM2F on
Sync interface 2 fault. Same actions as IFM1F.
EXTF on
External fault (module or field). Read diagnostic buffer and OB82 data.
INTF on
Internal fault (program or timing). Read buffer; correct program or cycle settings.
BUSF1 or BUSF2 on
Bus fault on that interface. Check cable, termination and slave power.

runbook.title: Redundancy sync troubleshooting
rows: Standby stuck in STARTUP
Compare firmware and project versions; repeat link-up.
Link-up rejected
Check that load memory matches; cycle time may be too long for link-up.
Frequent resync
Check fiber bend radius and connectors; replace sync module.
Switchover over 50 ms
Review min I/O retention time, cycle time and DP bus cycle.
Unexpected switchover
Read the diagnostic buffer for hardware fault or watchdog cause.
Download in RUN refused
Compile consistently; do a full download in STOP if needed.
Outputs flicker on switchover
Check output modules, Y-Link and slave fail-safe settings.
CPU times differ
Fix time synchronization source and set time-of-day on both CPUs.

runbook.title: Alkylation and Aromatic loop handling
rows: Trip and safety loops
Never bypass without approved MOC and operations sign-off.
Temperature and pressure controllers
Hold last output in manual during tie-in; confirm bumpless return.
Control valves
Verify fail action against the P&ID; test at 0, 50 and 100%.
Cutover order
Spare loops, non-critical, then critical; one group at a time.
Legacy wiring
Keep tagged and intact until SAT passes.
Analyzer loops
Check scaling with the lab; hold values during analyzer maintenance.
Hazardous-area loops
Re-verify IS barrier and entity parameters after cutover.
Rollback
Agree decision point first; reconnect legacy terminals and log it.

docTitle: Aradet SCADA Revamp - PCS 7 Execution Guide
description: SCADA engineer step-by-step execution guide for the Alkylation and Aromatic control system revamp (Aradet, Iraq).
ioLoopsNote: Starter example tags only. Replace with the real I/O schedule using CSV import (columns: tag, description, type AI/AO/DI/DO).

topology.note: Edit nodes, links, labels, paths, services and faults here for other topologies (S7-1500H, AVEVA). A service is lost when every path in it is blocked; one fault = BUMPLESS, two or more with service intact = DEGRADED, any service lost = CRITICAL.

services.lossText: Loss of I/O: neither Rack 0 (Line A) nor Rack 1 (Line B) can reach the field bus.
Loss of view: both OS servers are offline, so no operator view or archiving.

faults.name: CPU-0 rack failure
faults.expected: CPU-1 takes over as master with no process upset.
steps: Pull power on rack 0 or set CPU-0 to STOP
Confirm CPU-1 LED shows master and REDF is off
Check outputs held steady and OB72/OB82 entries logged
Restore rack 0; run resync and confirm return to redundant mode

faults.name: CPU-1 rack failure
faults.expected: Rack 0 path (Line A) stays master; Line B has no controller driving it.
steps: Pull power on rack 1 or set CPU-1 to STOP
Confirm CPU-0 stays master and the outputs hold steady
Check OB72 entries and REDF on the surviving CPU
Restore rack 1; run resync and confirm redundant mode

faults.name: PROFIBUS line A break
faults.expected: Traffic continues on line B; diagnostic alarm raised.
steps: Disconnect line A at an OLM or Y-Link
Confirm OB86 and OB122 diagnostics are raised
Confirm all slaves stay in data exchange on line B
Reconnect and verify redundancy restored with no stale values

faults.name: PROFIBUS line B break
faults.expected: Line A carries all traffic; diagnostic alarm raised and redundancy reported lost.
steps: Disconnect line B at an OLM or Y-Link
Confirm OB86/OB70 diagnostics are raised
Confirm all slaves stay in data exchange on line A
Reconnect and verify redundancy restored

faults.name: OS Server A offline
faults.expected: Clients switch to OS_SRV_B; archive gap is backfilled on return.
steps: Stop the WinCC runtime or power off OS_SRV_A
Confirm clients reconnect to OS_SRV_B
Check alarms still arrive and tag values update
Restart A; confirm archive synchronization completes

faults.name: OS Server B offline
faults.expected: Clients stay on OS_SRV_A; archive gap on B is backfilled on return.
steps: Stop WinCC runtime or power off OS_SRV_B
Confirm clients and alarms stay on OS_SRV_A
Restart B; confirm archive synchronization completes

faults.name: SCALANCE ring port break
faults.expected: MRP closes the ring within the configured recovery time (bumpless only if that time is below the AS/OS communication tolerance).
steps: Unplug one ring cable between two SCALANCE switches
Confirm MRP manager reports ring open and recovery in SINEC NMS
Verify no OS client or AS packet loss during recovery
Reconnect; confirm ring is closed and the trap clears
